case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Harihar Bux Singh and Another
respondent:
Harihar Bux Singh and Another
Supreme Court of India

13 August 1974
Cr.A. No. 14 of 1974.
The Judgment was delivered by: KHANNA, J.
1.  Harihar Bux Singh (62), his two sons Rudra Pratap Singh (30) and Mahesh Pratap Singh (27) and their employee Ram Singh (45) were tried in the Court of Civil and Sessions Judge Hardoi in connection with the murder of Hargovind Singh alias Lalla Singh (45). The learned Sessions Judge convicted Harihar Bux Singh u/s. 303 Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to death. Rudra Pratap Singh was convicted u/s. 302 Indian Penal Code. He too was sentenced to death. Mahesh Pratap Singh and Ram Singh were convicted u/s. 302 read with S. 34 Indian Penal Code and each of them was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life. On appeal and reference, the Allahabad High Court acquired all the four accused. The State of Uttar Pradesh has now filed the present appeal by special leave against Harihar Bux Singh and Rudra Pratap Singh.

facts: Harihar Bux Singh (62), his two sons Rudra Pratap Singh (30) and Mahesh Pratap Singh (27) and their employee Ram Singh (45) were tried in the Court of Civil and Sessions Judge Hardoi in connection with the murder of Hargovind Singh alias Lalla Singh (45).
The learned Sessions Judge convicted Harihar Bux Singh u/s. 303 Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to death.
Rudra Pratap Singh was convicted u/s. 302 Indian Penal Code.
He too was sentenced to death.
Mahesh Pratap Singh and Ram Singh were convicted u/s. 302 read with S. 34 Indian Penal Code and each of them was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life.
On appeal and reference, the Allahabad High Court acquitted all the four accused.
The State of Uttar Pradesh has now filed the present appeal by special leave against Harihar Bux Singh and Rudra Pratap Singh.
issues: Whether the conviction of the accused was based on reliable evidence?
petitioner_arguments: No case has been made for interference with the judgment of the High Court.
The fact that another view could also have been taken on the evidence on record would not justify interference with the judgment of acquittal.
respondent_arguments: Rajeshwari Devi's testimony was vitiated by a number of infirmities.
There was no motive proved on the record.
The allegation that there had been a dispute between Harihar Bux Singh accused and the deceased regarding partition of properties was found to be without basis.
court_reasoning: The High Court discussed her evidence at great length and found the same to be vitiated by a number of infirmities.
It was further held that there was no evidence of any quarrel between the children.
Another fact to which reference was made by the High Court was that Rajeshwari Devi had departed from her previous statement so that her version might not be belied by the medical evidence.
holding: The Appeal consequently fails and is dismissed.
